Title: Diagnosis of test `testKeepInitIfBest`

Details:
The test `testKeepInitIfBest` verifies that the optimizer correctly reports the best point found, even if it is the initially provided start value. The test defines a function `f` which is a sum of a sine function and a step function, designed so that the initial guess `init` might be the best point for minimization.

The test calls the `optimize` method of `BrentOptimizer` (which is a subclass of `BaseAbstractUnivariateOptimizer`) with the parameters including the initial start value. The relevant `optimize` method in `BaseAbstractUnivariateOptimizer` performs initial validations, sets various fields like `searchMin`, `searchMax`, `searchStart`, and then calls `doOptimize()` to perform the actual optimization.

From the snippets retrieved, the `optimize` method itself mostly sets up the boundaries and performs no optimization logic. The core optimization happens in `doOptimize()` (not yet reviewed).

The failure suggests that the algorithm might not be preserving the initial guess if it is the best value, or the search might start such that it misses or overrides this point.

Next step is to inspect the `doOptimize()` method implementation in `BrentOptimizer` or its base classes because this is where the core logic decides which points are evaluated and how the best point is updated.

I will now retrieve the `doOptimize()` method in `BrentOptimizer` or its superclass to investigate how it handles the initial guess and whether it preserves or discards it wrongly.

I will start with `doOptimize()` method in `BaseAbstractUnivariateOptimizer` since `optimize` is in that class and likely `doOptimize` is there too.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
